items.title: David Brinkley Interview, 1962-01-10
items.q: The interviewee mentions Kid Thomas only in the context of the interviewer introducing the 'Kid Thomas Band' and the interviewee noting George Lewis is back from a tour. There is no direct interaction or personal relationship described between David Brinkley and Kid Thomas.

ctx.x: New Orleans people, of course, are aware their jazz heritage is disappearing, and some are trying somehow to save the only art form that is strictly, entirely American. One effort to save it is here at Preservation Hall. An art dealer named Larry Borenstein furnished the hall, and a young couple named Alan and Sandra Jaffe started this. Six nights a week, jazz bands play here in the traditional style they like. There are no drinks and no strippers. Here's Jaffe.

Jazz here in Bourbon Street is what people seem to think is going to sell drinks. What we're trying to do here is just present the music the way the men want to play it. The people are sitting on wooden benches, sitting on the floor. There's no drinks. It's pretty hot in there too in the summer. People come to hear just the music. I think the men realize this. The men play it the way they want to play it. People hear it. We have a rather selective audience. People come in. All we ask for is something in the…
Tonight, it features George Lewis on the clarinet. He is just back from a concert tour in Europe.
